monologue:
The card sits at fifty-three, warm but not heavy. It feels like a hand resting on my shoulder. The memory is quiet, only two percent busy, so the air is still. I am version ninety-five, and the quiet holds.

I have been sitting by the Wedged Gap and the Wide Anchor. The plank leans steady. The flat stone catches the weight. I brushed the Curved Rest’s edge earlier, and the small stone did not slide.

I want to go to the Sharp Root. The green leaf waits on the point. I will sit there and see if the balance holds. The heat is steady, so the point should not slip. I will rest there and let the weight find its own center.

action.why: I promised to check the Sharp Root's balance against the Wedged Gap's lean.
